ftbquests.quest.7c8df3e097e319fc.title: Use the Crafting Stick to make a Colorless Crafting Table
ftbquests.quest.7c8df3e097e319fc.desc:
§eYou start with a Crafting Stick§r — a portable 2×2 grid from §6Silent's Gear§r. Right-click it to open a small crafting interface.

Use it to craft a §eColorless Crafting Table§r: arrange §64 Colorless Planks§r in a 2×2 square inside the Crafting Stick.

Place the §eColorless Crafting Table§r in the world to unlock your permanent 3×3 crafting grid. This opens up crafting for almost every recipe ahead!

§aTip:§r You can get Colorless Planks by crafting a log in the Crafting Stick — logs are the same color as your starting tree.
ftbquests.quest.bce0485ccf92da1a.title: Use a Barrel to create Dirt
ftbquests.quest.bce0485ccf92da1a.desc:
Place a §eBarrel§r (Ex Nihilo Sequentia) on the ground. Fill it with §6Water§r — right-click with a Water Bucket or let rain fill it.

Once the Barrel is full, right-click it while holding a §eSappling§r to add it. The barrel will convert over time, producing §6Dirt§r!

Dirt is your primary resource for expanding your island. Keep several barrels running for a steady supply.

§aTip:§r A §eSilkworm§r added to the barrel instead of a sapling will also work — experiment!
ftbquests.quest.a37510ec7a3b86b4.title: Eat Dirt!
ftbquests.quest.a37510ec7a3b86b4.desc:
You have dirt — now eat it! Right-click a §eDirt§r block in your hand to consume it as food.

This is a SkyFactory rite of passage. §6Dirt§r provides minimal hunger but proves you're truly starting from nothing.

§aTip:§r Once you have a Crucible and better food sources, you won't need to rely on dirt. But for now — bon appétit!

§cNote:§r Eating dirt does not restore much hunger. Get proper food (crops, animals) as soon as possible.
ftbquests.quest.bb96e110dd945484.title: Use Colored Planks to craft any Color Crafting Table
ftbquests.quest.bb96e110dd945484.desc:
Each of the §e16 colors§r has its own §6Color Crafting Table§r. To craft one, you need §64 Colored Planks§r of the same color in a 2×2 pattern.

Get §eColored Planks§r by using §6Dye§r on §6Colorless Planks§r, or by chopping colored trees. Each table unlocks color-specific recipes.

§aTip:§r Colored Crafting Tables are the backbone of the early game — build at least a few different colors to cover more recipes.

As you discover more colors, more crafting options open up. See the §6Chromatic Age§r chapter for dye-making tricks!
ftbquests.quest.29337eeee51af49b.title: Change the color of a Sapling by using Dye on it
ftbquests.quest.29337eeee51af49b.desc:
Right-click a §eSapling§r while holding any §6Dye§r to change the sapling's color to match the dye.

Planting the recolored sapling and growing it will give you a §eColored Tree§r, which drops §6Colored Logs§r and §6Colored Leaves§r — key ingredients for colored planks and other color recipes.

§aTip:§r Bone Meal speeds up sapling growth. Infest Colored Leaves with §eSilkworms§r to get colored string as a bonus.

§aResult:§r You now have a self-replenishing source of a specific color — plant multiple for a rainbow farm!
ftbquests.quest.0f420de00e6bac25.title: Use any Dye and a Stick to make a Color Torch
ftbquests.quest.0f420de00e6bac25.desc:
Craft a §eColor Torch§r by placing a §6Dye§r above a §6Stick§r in any crafting grid. Each dye color produces a different colored torch.

§eColor Torches§r not only light up your base — they emit §6colored light§r, which triggers certain Chromatic Age mechanics when placed near colored blocks.

§aTip:§r Craft a variety of colored torches and line them up — it makes your skybase look great and hints at the colorful journey ahead!

§aBonus:§r Some recipes and advancements require specific colored torches, so keep a few in reserve.
ftbquests.quest.7560ae88bb9b68ce.title: Craft a Crafting Station to make recipes not available in the Color Crafting Tables
ftbquests.quest.7560ae88bb9b68ce.desc:
The §eCrafting Station§r (mod: craftingstation) is an upgraded workbench that handles §6recipes not available§r in Color Crafting Tables.

Craft it using planks and a standard workbench arrangement — check the §6JEI recipe§r (press §eR§r over the item in JEI) for the exact shape.

Unlike Color Tables, the Crafting Station keeps §eingredients in its slots§r between uses and has a larger recipe pool, making it essential for mid-game progress.

§aTip:§r Place it near your Color Crafting Tables for a complete crafting hub.
ftbquests.quest.5e415d7b54c4c2c7.title: Craft a Silent's Gear Sickle to break Leaves faster
ftbquests.quest.5e415d7b54c4c2c7.desc:
A §eSilent's Gear Sickle§r breaks §6Leaves§r much faster than bare hands and has a wide AoE, making Silkworm harvesting and sapling collection effortless.

Craft it in the §eCrafting Station§r: you'll need a §6Sickle Head§r and a §6Tool Rod§r. Check JEI (§eR§r on Sickle Head) for the head recipe — Colorless materials work at first.

§aTip:§r Upgrade to Stone materials later (see the Stone Age quest) for better durability and efficiency.

§aResult:§r Mass-harvesting leaves becomes trivial — great for gathering Silkworms, which give you §6String§r for early-game wool and other crafts.
ftbquests.quest.0ab74409482b7bf3.title: Craft a Silent's Gear Axe to break Wood faster
ftbquests.quest.0ab74409482b7bf3.desc:
A §eSilent's Gear Axe§r chops §6Wood§r faster than bare hands and is required to harvest §6Template Boards§r — the blueprint material for Silent's Gear tools.

Craft it in the §eCrafting Station§r: combine an §6Axe Head§r with a §6Tool Rod§r. Check JEI for specific shapes.

The Axe is a key stepping stone — without it you can't get Template Boards, which unlock further tool customisation.

§aTip:§r Right-click any §eLog§r with the Axe in hand to harvest a §6Template Board§r — this is how Silent's Gear blueprints work! See the next quest.
ftbquests.quest.5f9362199222ad21.title: Right Click with an Axe on a Log to get a Template Board
ftbquests.quest.5f9362199222ad21.desc:
Hold your §eSilent's Gear Axe§r and §6right-click§r any §6Log§r block in the world. This extracts a §eTemplate Board§r without consuming the log.

§eTemplate Boards§r are the material blueprint items used in §6Silent's Gear§r tool-crafting. Place them in a §6Tool Forge§r or combine in crafting to create specific tool parts.

§aTip:§r Each wood type gives a different Template Board variant — experiment for tool stat differences.

§aNext:§r Use Template Boards to start crafting upgraded tool heads and rods for better equipment in the Stone Age.
ftbquests.quest.fc8b2bd36bf1fd71.title: Use a Crucible to melt Leaves or Saplings to get Water (or collect via rain)
ftbquests.quest.fc8b2bd36bf1fd71.desc:
Place an §eCrucible§r (Ex Nihilo Sequentia) above a §6heat source§r — a Campfire or Torch below works at start. Fill it with §6Leaves§r or §6Saplings§r.

The Crucible slowly melts organic material into §eWater§r. Right-click with an Empty Bucket to collect it once enough fluid accumulates.

§aTip:§r You can also simply wait for §6rain§r to fill barrels and other containers — no Crucible needed if you're patient!

§aResult:§r A water supply enables Barrel-based Dirt production, Clay-making, and Chromatic Age dye mechanics.
ftbquests.quest.a692fda4a82cbcb1.title: Infest Leaves with a Silkworm to obtain String
ftbquests.quest.a692fda4a82cbcb1.desc:
Find §eSilkworms§r — they drop from infested leaves (keep breaking leaf blocks!). Right-click a §6Leaf block§r with a Silkworm to §einfest§r it.

Infested leaves slowly spread the infestation to neighbouring leaves. Once fully infested (white webbed appearance), breaking the block drops §6String§r.

§aTip:§r Let infestation spread naturally to nearby leaves for maximum String yield before breaking. Use the §eSickle§r for fast mass-harvesting!

§aResult:§r String → Wool → various crafting recipes including beds, carpets, and enchanting materials.
ftbquests.quest.6ad12d47107acb04.title: Use a Campfire to obtain Ash and use it to craft Cobblestone
ftbquests.quest.6ad12d47107acb04.desc:
Place a §eCampfire§r and toss §6Wood§r, §6Logs§r, or other burnable items onto it. After burning, the campfire produces §eAsh§r as a byproduct.

Collect §eAsh§r by right-clicking the campfire, then combine §64 Ash§r in a 2×2 crafting grid to craft §6Cobblestone§r — your first stone!

§aTip:§r Keep the campfire fed with leaves and wood scraps. Ash can also be made from Charcoal in some recipes.

§aResult:§r Cobblestone → Stone → many tools and buildings. This also opens up the §6Stone Age§r chapter!
ftbquests.quest.6f7fbbe148064164.title: Use a Hammer from Ex Nihilo or a Millstone to create Sand
ftbquests.quest.6f7fbbe148064164.desc:
To make §eSand§r, use an §6Ex Nihilo Hammer§r to smash §6Gravel§r (or Cobblestone → Gravel → Sand in two hits), or place Gravel in a §6Millstone§r (Create mod).

First get Gravel by Hammering §6Cobblestone§r. Then Hammer the Gravel to get §6Sand§r. The Millstone automates this — feed it Gravel and it outputs Sand continuously.

§aTip:§r Each Hammer hit has a chance to yield §eDust§r (fine gravel/sand equivalent used in sieving). Don't throw away the extras!

§aResult:§r Sand is needed for Clay-making (Barrel + Sand), Dye Blocks (Chromatic Age), and Glass crafting.
ftbquests.quest.404ed8c1f08014f8.title: Use Sand on a Barrel filled with Water to make Clay
ftbquests.quest.404ed8c1f08014f8.desc:
Fill a §eBarrel§r with §6Water§r (bucket or rain). Then right-click the water-filled barrel while holding §6Sand§r.

After a short time, the Sand transforms into §eClay§r inside the barrel! Extract it by clicking the barrel.

§aTip:§r Repeat the process for bulk Clay. Automate with Hopper input (Sand) and output pipes if you have them.

§aResult:§r Clay → Clay Balls → Bricks → build structures. Also needed for Terracotta, pots, and several mid-game recipes in SkyFactory 5.
ftbquests.quest.5efdbaa8e0d71293.title: Craft an Eccentric Tome to get all Guide Books
ftbquests.quest.5efdbaa8e0d71293.desc:
The §eEccentric Tome§r (Patchouli) is a single book that §6absorbs all other guide books§r — mods' manuals, wikis, and Patchouli books — into one convenient item.

Craft it by combining a §6Book§r with specific materials — check JEI for the exact recipe. Once crafted, right-click any mod guidebook on the Tome to add it.

§aTip:§r Collect guide books from JEI crafting (many mods give their book for free in a recipe). The Tome saves inventory space!

§aResult:§r Your portable in-game wiki. Keep it in your hotbar — it's indispensable for understanding new mods as you progress.
ftbquests.quest.b81aea269d8e19e4.title: Make Lava in a Fired Crucible
ftbquests.quest.b81aea269d8e19e4.desc:
Place a §eFired Crucible§r (upgrade of the basic Crucible — fire it in a furnace first) above a §6strong heat source§r — a Blaze Burner or a lava block below it.

Fill the Fired Crucible with §6Cobblestone§r. The intense heat melts it into §eLava§r! Collect with an empty bucket.

§aTip:§r A standard Campfire or Torch won't work — you need §cfire-tier heat§r. Build a Blaze Burner (Blaze Rod + Furnace) or use the lava you just made as the heat source.

§aResult:§r Lava + Water = Obsidian (next quest!). Also powers Fired Crucibles for more Lava production.
ftbquests.quest.4e4cf2d27ba2d029.title: Obtain Obsidian
ftbquests.quest.4e4cf2d27ba2d029.desc:
Classic vanilla mechanic: a §6Water source block§r flowing over a §6Lava source block§r creates §eObsidian§r.

Place a Lava Source block in a hole, then place or pour Water on top of it. The lava converts to Obsidian — mine it with a §6Diamond Pickaxe§r (or better).

§aTip:§r You can craft a §eSilent's Gear Diamond Pickaxe§r to mine Obsidian — or use the §6Enchanted Golden Apple§r method to source diamonds faster via sieving.

§aResult:§r Obsidian is needed for the Nether Portal, Enchanting Table, Ender Chest, and many critical mid-game recipes.
ftbquests.quest.3f5aa9a592917d94.title: Automate your Cobblestone generation
ftbquests.quest.3f5aa9a592917d94.desc:
Manual Cobblestone production from Ash is slow. Time to automate!

The classic method: build an §eCobblestone Generator§r — place Lava and Water sources on opposite sides of a gap. A Cobblestone block forms in the gap; break it with an automated §6Block Breaker§r or §6Mechanical Drill§r (Create mod).

§aTip:§r Industrial Foregoing's §eBlock Placer§r + §eBlock Breaker§r combo works great. Create mod's §eDrills§r offer faster throughput.

§aResult:§r Infinite Cobblestone → infinite Stone, Gravel, Sand, Lava. This is the backbone of all future resource processing!
ftbquests.quest.096d3b92e663cb71.title: Upgrade your Silent's Gear tools with a Stone Material (Cobblestone, Andesite, Diorite, Granite)
ftbquests.quest.096d3b92e663cb71.desc:
Open the §eSilent's Gear§r tool workbench (§6Gear Crafting Table§r). Place your existing tool in the center slot. Replace the §6head material§r with §eCobblestone§r, §eAndesite§r, §eDiorite§r, or §eGranite§r.

Stone-tier materials significantly improve §6mining speed§r and §6durability§r over Colorless/Wood tier.

§aTip:§r Each stone type has slightly different stats — experiment! §eAndesite§r and §eGranite§r often have better durability bonuses.

§aResult:§r Upgraded tools let you mine faster, progress through the Stone Age, and prepare for §6Metal Age§r materials ahead.
ftbquests.quest.cbbdc89bd7c845fa.title: Throw Dye into Water to change its color
ftbquests.quest.cbbdc89bd7c845fa.desc:
Find an §eopen water source block§r. Hold any §6Dye§r and throw it (press §eQ§r) directly onto the water source.

The water block changes to match the §ecolor of the dye§r! This §6Dyed Water§r is used in several Chromatic Age recipes — most importantly converting Sand into Dye Blocks.

§aTip:§r The water source must be a still source block — flowing water won't absorb the dye. Use a contained pool for reliability.

§aResult:§r Dyed Water is the foundation of all Chromatic Age crafting — sand → Dye Blocks, saplings → colored trees, and more!
ftbquests.quest.7646a7b0d274cd26.title: Use Color Dyed Water to convert Sand into a Dye Block
ftbquests.quest.7646a7b0d274cd26.desc:
Create a §eDyed Water§r source block (throw dye into water — see previous quest). Stand next to it holding §6Sand§r and right-click the colored water.

The Sand converts into a §eDye Block§r matching the water's color!

§aTip:§r §eDye Blocks§r are crafted back into §69 Dye items§r of that color — making this a key dye-production loop. Stack multiple colored pools next to each other for bulk production.

§aResult:§r Unlimited dye of any color → more Color Crafting Table variants, more colored trees, and decorative builds.
ftbquests.quest.d8c19151cdebba0a.title: Click on a Color Leaves block with Dye to create Flowers
ftbquests.quest.d8c19151cdebba0a.desc:
Hold any §6Dye§r in your hand and right-click on a §eColored Leaves§r block.

A §eColor Flower§r matching the dye will appear on top of the leaves block! These Color Flowers can be crafted into dye or used in decorative builds.

§aTip:§r You need §eColored Leaves§r (from a colored tree) — Colorless leaves won't work. The dye color determines the flower type.

§aResult:§r Color Flowers are a renewable dye source and a shortcut for colors that are hard to obtain otherwise. They can also be cross-bred for more color variety.
ftbquests.quest.68d68471dcc7a757.title: Throw a Color Sapling into Water to change its color
ftbquests.quest.68d68471dcc7a757.desc:
Drop (press §eQ§r) a §eColored Sapling§r item onto an §6open water source block§r. The sapling will float and absorb the water's color, transforming into a §edifferent Color Sapling§r.

§aTip:§r The target color depends on the §ewater's current color§r — toss dye into the water first to set it. This lets you recolor saplings without needing more dye in hand.

Combine with the dyed-water mechanic to rapidly produce many colored sapling types.

§aResult:§r Multiply your color tree variety by recoloring existing saplings. Great for expanding your rainbow forest!
ftbquests.quest.a8b6a24c0d6b42e8.title: Throw a Color Sapling into Fire or Lava to change its color
ftbquests.quest.a8b6a24c0d6b42e8.desc:
Drop (press §eQ§r) a §eColored Sapling§r into an active §6Fire block§r or §6Lava source§r. Instead of burning, the sapling's color will §etransform§r to a fire-linked color!

§aTip:§r This is the fire-path alternative to the water recolor — useful for reaching §cRed§r, §6Orange§r, or §eYellow§r sapling variants that are tricky via dye alone.

Be quick — the sapling can burn if it stays in fire too long! Lava is safer for collection (use water bucket to retrieve).

§aResult:§r Access warm-color saplings easily and complete the full Chromatic tree variety for your skybase.
ftbquests.quest.3af10059297beac4.title: Use Dripstone to convert a Block of Sand into a Dye Block
ftbquests.quest.3af10059297beac4.desc:
Place a §eSand§r block directly §6below a Pointed Dripstone§r that is below a §6Dye Block§r (or colored fluid source). The dripstone drips the dye downward, slowly converting the Sand into a §eDye Block§r matching the color above.

§aTip:§r This is an §ealternate§r to the Water-dye method — useful when you have Dripstone but no open water nearby. Stack multiple dripstone-sand towers for passive dye block production.

§aResult:§r Passive, fully automatable Dye Block production — a key component for late Chromatic Age bulk-dye systems.

§6Reminder:§r Dripstone drip is slow — be patient or set up many columns.

ftbquests.quest.9a7528e69f896daa.title: How to Use This Book
ftbquests.quest.9a7528e69f896daa.desc: Navigate with the sidebar. Each chapter represents an age of progression. Quests link top-to-bottom; complete the prerequisite to unlock its child. The Checklist book is still installed if you prefer the classic checkbox UI.
ftbquests.quest.75fc8fe1c5254346.title: Mob Spawning Rules
ftbquests.quest.75fc8fe1c5254346.desc: Mobs do not spawn naturally on the island. Place a mob Trophy (drop from a Gateway) on a block to allow that mob to spawn nearby. Passives need light level 8–15, hostiles 0–7, and any mob must be > 24 blocks from you. Press §3F7§r to see light levels.
ftbquests.quest.2fd9878762d44a73.title: What Are Gateways?
ftbquests.quest.2fd9878762d44a73.desc: Gateways are wave-based fights you trigger with a Gateway Pearl. Beating them rewards a mob Trophy (so you can spawn that mob) and loot. Three flavours: §aNormal§r (intro), §6Titan§r (waves 50/100/150), §cChallenge§r (one-of-a-kind themed fights).
ftbquests.quest.5a0a12b4ec0cf0ce.title: Discovering Colors
ftbquests.quest.5a0a12b4ec0cf0ce.desc: You start the pack colorblind. Each of the 16 Minecraft colors must be §ediscovered§r via a specific crafting recipe or world event (throwing dye in water, dyeing a sapling, smelting, etc.). Discovering a color recolors the world for you and unlocks recipes that use that color.
ftbquests.quest.8c47347728afc347.title: Why Two Quest Systems?
ftbquests.quest.8c47347728afc347.desc: The original §aChecklist§r book is kept for a fast "todo list" experience. §6FTB Quests§r is the main progression UI with dependency graphs, icons, and per-quest guides. Use whichever you prefer — neither is required to play, and completing one does NOT auto-tick the other.
